record.original_question: For a given field F, which finite groups G are F-admissible, meaning that there exists a G-crossed-product F-division algebra?

evidence.quote: Problem 11.1. Determine which groups are F-admissible, for a field F.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $F$ be a field. A finite group $G$ is called $F$-admissible if there exists a central division algebra $D$ over $F$ that is a $G$-crossed product; equivalently, $D$ contains a maximal subfield $L$ such that $L/F$ is a Galois extension with $\mathrm{Gal}(L/F) \cong G$.

Problem: For an arbitrary field $F$, determine (characterize intrinsically) the class of finite groups $G$ that are $F$-admissible. In particular, give necessary and sufficient conditions on a finite group $G$ for it to be realizable as the Galois group of a maximal subfield of some finite-dimensional central division algebra over $F$.
artifact.category_tag: Admissible groups and crossed product division algebras
artifact.status_search_result: The general problem of characterizing $F$-admissible groups remains open. Schacher (1968) proved that every $\mathbb{Q}$-admissible group has metacyclic Sylow subgroups, and the converse — the $\mathbb{Q}$-admissibility conjecture — is still open in general, though many partial results exist (e.g. for solvable groups by Sonn, and recent work on number fields including the 2024 preprint "Admissible groups over number fields"). No complete characterization is known for arbitrary $F$.

status_evidence.title: Open problems on Central Simple Algebras
status_evidence.snippet: Problem 11.1. Determine which groups are F-admissible, for a field F.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is explicitly listed as an open problem on central simple algebras.

status_evidence.title: Admissible Groups over Number Fields
status_evidence.snippet: We give a complete classification ... characterizations of admissible groups over several classes of number fields
status_evidence.claim: As of 2024 the admissibility problem is still being actively studied with only partial classifications even over number fields.

status_evidence.title: Sylow-metacyclic groups and Q-admissibility
status_evidence.snippet: Q-admissibility conjecture asserts every group with metacyclic Sylow subgroups is Q-admissible
status_evidence.claim: The Q-admissibility conjecture remains open, indicating the general F-admissibility problem is unsolved.
